text.p: These are the leading stories in Zimbabwe's state-owned Herald newspaper on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Britain has, in a major show of confidence with Zimbabwe's efforts to reform the economy, agreed in principle to cancel short-term debt which the government estimates could exceed Z$280 million.
- Zimtrade chief executive Morrison Sifelani has resigned in circumstances which remain shrouded in uncertainty.

- The beleaguered executive secretary of the Common Market of East and Southern Africa (Comesa), Bingu wa Mutharika, has refused to cooperate with an investigation team set up by the Council of Ministers to investigate various complaints made against him, according to sources.
- The Post and Telecommunications Corporation last week cut the telex lines rented by national news agency Ziana, for non-payment of fees.

- European representatives of a consortium of banks are in Harare for discussions with the government on the financial arrangements for the new Harare International Airport terminal building, sources said.
